core.abstract: Generative inverse design of three-dimensional structures combines a learned geometry representation with diffusion proposals and optimization-based constraint refinement.

正文数学符号提取发生错序，并遗漏无量纲长度的上横线。原页可读为λ_g=[L̄,N,m]及W(x,λ_L,λ_g)，几何样本数量为N_geo=47,800。已纠正；涉及几何参数定义和场表示，非原文缺项。

图5内部坐标、训练轮数和细节标签未进入文字提取。原页可读出图5a的两个MSE坐标及50,000、20,000 epochs标注，图5b的过拟合和边缘保持对比标签，以及W/m色标。已补读；遗漏影响训练比较和几何保真性证据的理解，并非原文件缺图。
图6内部的曲线、代表结果标注、UMAP标签及分布图图例未进入文字提取，已据原页补读。图6c图例包括25%—75%、1.5IQR范围、中位数、最大或最小值，不能将全部图形范围解释为标准差。遗漏影响分布统计与生成结果的理解，非原文件缺项。
表1的文字提取未完整保留合并单元格关系。原页上半部分固定生成数量为1000、改变聚类数量；下半部分固定聚类数量为5、改变生成数量。脚注限定统计对象为聚类代表。已核对并恢复对应关系，避免将0.9579误认为所有实验条件下恒定的最大r²。
图7的实际样本量、误差棒定义及相对标准误差标注未进入文字提取。原页明确P1—P5样本量为10、9、2、9、10，误差棒为SEM，RSE=SEM/mean×100%；P3装填率和长度的RSE为12%和11%。已补读，避免将10次总实验误认为每种模式均有10个样本，或将排除P3后的低于3%结论推广到全部模式。
图8内部数值及曲线标签未进入文字提取，已据原页补读。五种模式最终r²依次为0.9881、0.9935、0.9801、0.9877、0.9796；其中P5为0.9796，不应四舍五入后表述为严格超过0.98。右侧三类目标项的黑、红、蓝对应关系与图注一致。遗漏影响最终匹配程度的准确理解，非原文件缺项。
图9内部12组曲线、结构图及r²、η标注未进入文字提取，已据原页补读。例如案例i为r²=0.9457、η=98.1%，案例g为r²=0.983、η=70.3%。这些结果不能概括为所有案例r²均超过0.98或装填率均超过75%；遗漏影响跨案例性能与约束达成情况的判断。
图10内部的数值、图例及比较标注未进入文字提取，已据原页补读。在η=82.6%处，本文结果r²=0.9943，MENN比较结果r²=0.9924；阴影为分箱后的±1标准差，不是置信区间。遗漏影响重复比较的量化理解，非原文件缺项。
图11内部的目标函数、局部几何标注、三组结果及近邻说明未进入文字提取。原页目标函数包含性能匹配、装填率、eikonal残差及三类局部几何惩罚项；三个结果旁均展示“Five neighbors in dataset”。已补读，遗漏影响约束微调与数据集近邻比较的理解；未发现公式占位或原文件缺项。
式(5)的分式、求和范围与下标在文字提取中错序。原页为N_i=N_geo·DOF_i/(Σ_{j=1}^{N_type}DOF_j)，i=1,…,N_type。已核对，影响按自由度分配各类型样本数的理解，非原文件缺项。
图12a图注的球形类别被提取为“2 types of spherical grains”，原页清楚写为“3 types of spherical grains”，已按原页纠正。图12内部网格分类及数据组成也未完整进入文字提取，已补读。
图12a图注原页列出10、3、4、5、10、2、3、6类，合计43，但同时称总数为42。属于已核实的原页计数不一致，而非页面不清；现有资料不能确定哪个分项应修正，影响几何类型组成的准确复核，不影响本页现有内容识读。
式(6)的分段结构、上下标及矩阵行列在文字提取中混乱。原页明确潜向量和几何向量随同一几何的重复采样保持对应，性能矩阵第一行为时间、第二行为压力。已核对，避免将采样次数误当几何数量或将两行矩阵误读为单一向量。
式(7)—(11)的权重、积分、范数及上下标在文字提取中部分错序。原页式(9)显示F_η=(1−η)²；式(10)被积项为(1−‖∇_xW‖)²；式(11)积分下标是边界标记，非偏导算子。均已据原页纠正，影响目标函数和物理残差的准确理解；未发现缺失公式。
式(12)、(13)的积分范围、分段括号、分母及平方位置在文字提取中错序。原页可明确区分式(12)中u的分段定义、对y的偏导与平面边界积分，以及式(13)的线边界积分。已核对，影响几何惩罚项含义；原页未缺公式。
“Measures of performance matching degree”首段在原页将计算曲线和目标曲线均标为p_T(t)，而式(14)—(16)明确分别使用p(t)和p_T(t)。属于原文符号误标，不是提取错误；影响两条曲线的身份区分，但后续公式可读且无需补造。
式(14)—(16)的分式、指数、积分及向量括号在文字提取中错序。原页式(14)区分压力计算、肉厚随时间的积分以及等值燃面的面积定义；式(15)、(16)区分计算压力向量与目标压力向量。已据原页核对，未发现占位或缺项。
式(17)的文字提取遗漏目标均值的上横线并打乱点积结构。原页分子为(p_T−p)·(p_T−p)，分母为(p_T−p̄_T)·(p_T−p̄_T)，整体为1减该比值。已纠正，避免将归一化分母误读为零或将r²误解为普通相关系数的平方。
参考文献17在原页以“Defence Technology, (2025).”结束，未提供卷号、页码、文章号或DOI。该条书目信息不完整已由原页核实，但不能据此判断文献不存在或研究结论错误；影响精确定位与核验。无公式或图号涉及，页面仍可阅读。

core.title: Toward Intelligent Fatigue Management of Welded Metal Sheet Structures by Integrating Simulation, Sensing, and Machine Learning
core.abstract: Welded metal sheets are used across automotive, aerospace, marine, and civil infrastructure applications for their high strength and light weight, yet fatigue failure remains a persistent concern in relation to their long-term structural stability. Fatigue crack growth is strongly influenced by the interaction of weld geometry and manufacturing-related defects. This review presents a comprehensive overview of fatigue-life prediction approaches, outlining the welding processes, fatigue mechanisms, computational tools, and progress made in predictive approaches central to this field. Fatigue performance is evaluated across several welding approaches, including laser beam, resistance spot, tungsten inert gas, and hybrid laser–arc welding. Advanced computational approaches for predicting fatigue life, including finite element modeling, cohesive zone modeling, crystal plasticity modeling, and multi-physics/multi-scale simulation, are also examined. Recent innovations in experimental characterization and structural health monitoring are addressed in detail. The review further highlights how machine learning-enabled digital twins and sensor fusion frameworks improve fatigue damage detection and maintenance prediction. Unlike prior reviews that treat conventional and data-driven methods separately, this work integrates welding process selection, fatigue life prediction, experimental validation, and structural health monitoring within a single closed-loop simulation–sensing–machine learning framework specific to thin welded sheets. Despite such advancements, the accurate prediction of environmental degradation and microstructural evolution remains challenging, and future research is required to integrate physics-based and data-driven models for critical welded structures.

core.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Fatigue and Fracture Analysis and Prediction: A Scoping Review
core.abstract: Physics-Informed Machine Learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for fatigue and fracture analysis, combining the data-driven flexibility of neural networks with the consistency of physical laws. This scoping review maps the extent, range, and nature of research on PIML applied to fatigue life prediction, crack growth and propagation, multiaxial fatigue, damage mechanics, prognostics and health management, and structural health monitoring, covering the literature published from 2018 up to August 2026. A comprehensive search strategy integrated the core terminology of the field with broader synonym terms, complemented by forward and backward citation searching and manual screening of the most productive venues. The combined strategy retrieved 124 records, of which 76 primary research articles satisfied the inclusion criteria and were charted and characterized in this review. The included studies are characterized through the lens of a three-bias taxonomy—observational, learning, and inductive—which organizes how physical knowledge enters the learning pipeline: through data-level constraints, loss-function modifications, and structural architectural changes, respectively. The review maps the architectural landscape of the field, from standard multi-layer perceptron-based PINNs to specialized variants including sequential attention models, physics-informed Kolmogorov–Arnold networks, geometry-aware finite encodings, graph neural networks, and probabilistic Bayesian formulations. The mapped literature indicates that PIML methods are reported to improve generalization from sparse and noisy experimental data, achieve computational gains over conventional simulation, and quantify prediction uncertainty. Persistent challenges nonetheless emerge across the mapped literature, including high training costs, sensitivity to hyperparameter and loss-weighting choices, limited transferability across problem configurations, and the black-box nature of deep models. The review identifies knowledge gaps and concludes with an agenda for future research, emphasizing generalizable and adaptive architectures, multi-scale and multi-physics formulations, and standardized benchmarks.

extended.title: Concealing LLM-Based Multi-Agent Topology via Phantom Structure Injection
extended.abstract: Driven by the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs), LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for collaborative reasoning over complex tasks. A key design element of MAS is the communication topology, which governs information flow among agents and often encodes proprietary knowledge about the system architecture. However, recent work has shown that such topologies can be inferred even in black-box settings by exploiting semantic dependencies in observable reasoning traces, posing significant risks of intellectual property leakage and exposure of system vulnerabilities. To address this threat, we propose MIRAGE, a topology-concealment framework that preserves the genuine communication topology for task execution while shaping adversary-facing semantic evidence toward a carefully constructed phantom topology. Specifically, MIRAGE operates in three stages: (1) phantom topology synthesis, (2) semantic edge realization, and (3) protected MAS execution. It constructs a phantom topology structurally distinct from the genuine one, materializes phantom edges as plausible semantic dependencies, and suppresses source-specific cues that could reveal genuine edges absent from the phantom topology. Extensive experiments across three topology optimization frameworks and four benchmark datasets demonstrate that MIRAGE substantially reduces the effectiveness of topology inference attacks while largely preserving the task utility of the protected MAS.

extended.title: Performance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue deterioration subjected to TNT equivalent BLEVE loads
extended.abstract: During the service life, bridges are subjected to long-term fatigue loads induced by heavy-duty vehicles, while simultaneously facing the threat of accidental explosions resulting from warfare, improper transportation of hazardous materials, or traffic accidents. It is widely known that fatigue causes material damage and degradation of structural performance. Unfortunately, the accumulated fatigue damage has not been considered for estimating the dynamic behaviour of the bridge deck. This study proposes a numerical method to evaluate the blast resistance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue damage subjected to boiling liquid expanding vapour explosion (BLEVE) loads by the TNT equivalent method. First, the finite element models of T-beam bridge decks are established to analyse the influence of fatigue on their blast performance. The results indicate that fatigue significantly weakens the blast resistance of the T-beam bridge decks (with the mid-span displacement increasing by up to 2 times). This phenomenon is mainly attributed to the differences in the energy dissipation mechanisms. Second, parametric analysis indicates that TNT equivalence is the most sensitive parameter, with an amplification effect of up to 1.8 times. Finally, based on machine learning techniques optimised via 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, a predictive model for the maximum displacement of fatigue-damaged T-beam bridge decks under blast loading is established. This study provides a reliable and efficient approach for the damage assessment of long-term service bridges under blast loading.

papers.title: Toward Intelligent Fatigue Management of Welded Metal Sheet Structures by Integrating Simulation, Sensing, and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Welded metal sheets are used across automotive, aerospace, marine, and civil infrastructure applications for their high strength and light weight, yet fatigue failure remains a persistent concern in relation to their long-term structural stability. Fatigue crack growth is strongly influenced by the interaction of weld geometry and manufacturing-related defects. This review presents a comprehensive overview of fatigue-life prediction approaches, outlining the welding processes, fatigue mechanisms, computational tools, and progress made in predictive approaches central to this field. Fatigue performance is evaluated across several welding approaches, including laser beam, resistance spot, tungsten inert gas, and hybrid laser–arc welding. Advanced computational approaches for predicting fatigue life, including finite element modeling, cohesive zone modeling, crystal plasticity modeling, and multi-physics/multi-scale simulation, are also examined. Recent innovations in experimental characterization and structural health monitoring are addressed in detail. The review further highlights how machine learning-enabled digital twins and sensor fusion frameworks improve fatigue damage detection and maintenance prediction. Unlike prior reviews that treat conventional and data-driven methods separately, this work integrates welding process selection, fatigue life prediction, experimental validation, and structural health monitoring within a single closed-loop simulation–sensing–machine learning framework specific to thin welded sheets. Despite such advancements, the accurate prediction of environmental degradation and microstructural evolution remains challenging, and future research is required to integrate physics-based and data-driven models for critical welded structures.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Fatigue and Fracture Analysis and Prediction: A Scoping Review
papers.abstract: Physics-Informed Machine Learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for fatigue and fracture analysis, combining the data-driven flexibility of neural networks with the consistency of physical laws. This scoping review maps the extent, range, and nature of research on PIML applied to fatigue life prediction, crack growth and propagation, multiaxial fatigue, damage mechanics, prognostics and health management, and structural health monitoring, covering the literature published from 2018 up to August 2026. A comprehensive search strategy integrated the core terminology of the field with broader synonym terms, complemented by forward and backward citation searching and manual screening of the most productive venues. The combined strategy retrieved 124 records, of which 76 primary research articles satisfied the inclusion criteria and were charted and characterized in this review. The included studies are characterized through the lens of a three-bias taxonomy—observational, learning, and inductive—which organizes how physical knowledge enters the learning pipeline: through data-level constraints, loss-function modifications, and structural architectural changes, respectively. The review maps the architectural landscape of the field, from standard multi-layer perceptron-based PINNs to specialized variants including sequential attention models, physics-informed Kolmogorov–Arnold networks, geometry-aware finite encodings, graph neural networks, and probabilistic Bayesian formulations. The mapped literature indicates that PIML methods are reported to improve generalization from sparse and noisy experimental data, achieve computational gains over conventional simulation, and quantify prediction uncertainty. Persistent challenges nonetheless emerge across the mapped literature, including high training costs, sensitivity to hyperparameter and loss-weighting choices, limited transferability across problem configurations, and the black-box nature of deep models. The review identifies knowledge gaps and concludes with an agenda for future research, emphasizing generalizable and adaptive architectures, multi-scale and multi-physics formulations, and standardized benchmarks.

papers.title: Concealing LLM-Based Multi-Agent Topology via Phantom Structure Injection
papers.abstract: Driven by the rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs), LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a powerful paradigm for collaborative reasoning over complex tasks. A key design element of MAS is the communication topology, which governs information flow among agents and often encodes proprietary knowledge about the system architecture. However, recent work has shown that such topologies can be inferred even in black-box settings by exploiting semantic dependencies in observable reasoning traces, posing significant risks of intellectual property leakage and exposure of system vulnerabilities. To address this threat, we propose MIRAGE, a topology-concealment framework that preserves the genuine communication topology for task execution while shaping adversary-facing semantic evidence toward a carefully constructed phantom topology. Specifically, MIRAGE operates in three stages: (1) phantom topology synthesis, (2) semantic edge realization, and (3) protected MAS execution. It constructs a phantom topology structurally distinct from the genuine one, materializes phantom edges as plausible semantic dependencies, and suppresses source-specific cues that could reveal genuine edges absent from the phantom topology. Extensive experiments across three topology optimization frameworks and four benchmark datasets demonstrate that MIRAGE substantially reduces the effectiveness of topology inference attacks while largely preserving the task utility of the protected MAS.

papers.title: Performance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue deterioration subjected to TNT equivalent BLEVE loads
papers.abstract: During the service life, bridges are subjected to long-term fatigue loads induced by heavy-duty vehicles, while simultaneously facing the threat of accidental explosions resulting from warfare, improper transportation of hazardous materials, or traffic accidents. It is widely known that fatigue causes material damage and degradation of structural performance. Unfortunately, the accumulated fatigue damage has not been considered for estimating the dynamic behaviour of the bridge deck. This study proposes a numerical method to evaluate the blast resistance of T-beam bridge decks with fatigue damage subjected to boiling liquid expanding vapour explosion (BLEVE) loads by the TNT equivalent method. First, the finite element models of T-beam bridge decks are established to analyse the influence of fatigue on their blast performance. The results indicate that fatigue significantly weakens the blast resistance of the T-beam bridge decks (with the mid-span displacement increasing by up to 2 times). This phenomenon is mainly attributed to the differences in the energy dissipation mechanisms. Second, parametric analysis indicates that TNT equivalence is the most sensitive parameter, with an amplification effect of up to 1.8 times. Finally, based on machine learning techniques optimised via 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation, a predictive model for the maximum displacement of fatigue-damaged T-beam bridge decks under blast loading is established. This study provides a reliable and efficient approach for the damage assessment of long-term service bridges under blast loading.
